# Feature: Locator Engine & Auto-Wait

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-004
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan.md`

Yantra's **core reliability bet**: a Playwright-inspired locator engine implemented over `puppeteer-core`'s CDP transport. This is the layer that lets recorded workflows survive DOM drift — every logical target ("Sign in button", "Username field") is resolved against a **ranked candidate chain**, not a single brittle selector. The engine owns this resolution; the agent never invents selectors.

Concretely, this feature delivers:

1. **Deterministic locator resolution over candidate chains** — `LocatorResolver.resolve(chain)` walks ordered `LocatorCandidate`s in the page context, returning the first that resolves to **exactly one** element (strict mode by default). The Node-side coordinator never crosses the page boundary with raw DOM payloads — only `{objectId, count, used_candidate_index}` returns.
2. **Auto-wait until actionable** — repeats resolution until the target is visible (bounding rect > 0), stable (no position/animation change for 100ms), enabled (no `disabled` attribute or `aria-disabled`), and **receives events** (`elementFromPoint` at center hits the element or a descendant). Polling backoff borrowed wholesale from Playwright: `[0, 20, 50, 100, 100, 500, 500, 500, …]` ms within the layer-1 retry budget.
3. **Hit-target interception** — before any synthesized click, verify `elementFromPoint(cx, cy)` lands on the locator's element. If an overlay/modal/banner intercepts, fail fast with `HitTargetInterceptedError` (carrying the intercepting element's tag + accessible name) so the executor's layer-2 retry can attempt a different scroll alignment or surface the failure cleanly.
4. **Candidate ranking algorithm for record time** — given a captured DOM target, generate the top-N candidates ranked by stability + specificity. This is the algorithm FEAT-008's recorder will call to populate each named locator's chain. Ranking matches the plan/memory ordering: `data-testid > role+name > label-for > placeholder > unique CSS > relative anchor > absolute XPath`.

**Why this is the reliability bet**: `puppeteer-core` gives us CDP transport, targets, and `Runtime.evaluate`. It gives us nothing about _reliable element interaction_. Auto-wait, strict mode, hit-target verification, ARIA computed-role/name — every reliability property that makes Playwright workflows survive real-world DOM churn lives in this feature. Without it, FEAT-008 (recorder) and FEAT-010 (replay) regress to selector-roulette and the project's central value proposition collapses.

**Out of scope for this feature** (deferred to later features or Phase 2):

- LLM reanchor on chain exhaustion — Phase 2; MVP fails fast with a structured report.
- Composable selector syntax with `>>` pipe and engines like `internal:and`, `internal:or` — brainstorm §6.1 mentions these; this feature implements per-strategy resolution as discrete `LocatorCandidate` kinds, not a composed string DSL. The discriminated union is more strongly typed and aligns with the protocol's structured `LocatorChain`.
- Shadow DOM piercing, multi-frame `>>>` traversal, full ARIA tree snapshotting — explicitly skipped per brainstorm §6.5.
- `xpath` engine beyond the absolute-XPath last-resort candidate.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> Yantra is filesystem-native; there is no relational database in MVP. The "data model" here is the **in-memory entity graph** plus one **on-disk build artifact** and a **future-DB schema sketch** for analytics.

### In-Memory Entities

#### `LocatorIntent` — discriminated union, the typed intent for one candidate

```ts
type LocatorIntent =
  | { kind: 'role'; role: AriaRole; name?: string | RegExp; exact?: boolean }
  | { kind: 'testid'; attribute?: string; value: string } // default attribute: 'data-testid'
  | { kind: 'label'; text: string | RegExp; exact?: boolean } // <label for=…> / aria-labelledby / aria-label
  | { kind: 'placeholder'; text: string | RegExp; exact?: boolean }
  | { kind: 'text'; text: string | RegExp; exact?: boolean; normalize?: boolean }
  | { kind: 'css'; selector: string }
  | { kind: 'xpath'; expression: string }
  | { kind: 'relative'; anchor: LocatorIntent; relation: RelativeRelation; targetRole?: AriaRole };

type RelativeRelation =
  | 'next-sibling'
  | 'previous-sibling'
  | 'following'
  | 'preceding' // anywhere after / before in document order
  | 'ancestor'
  | 'descendant'
  | 'labeled-by'; // shorthand for label-for / aria-labelledby

type AriaRole =
  | 'button'
  | 'link'
  | 'textbox'
  | 'checkbox'
  | 'radio'
  | 'combobox'
  | 'listbox'
  | 'option'
  | 'tab'
  | 'tabpanel'
  | 'dialog'
  | 'alert'
  | 'heading'
  | 'img'
  | 'table'
  | 'row'
  | 'cell'
  | 'columnheader'
  | 'rowheader'
  | 'list'
  | 'listitem'
  | 'menu'
  | 'menuitem'
  | 'menubar'
  | 'navigation'
  | 'main'
  | 'banner'
  | 'contentinfo'
  | 'complementary'
  | 'search'
  | 'form'
  | 'region'
  | 'article'
  | 'switch'
  | 'progressbar'
  | 'slider'
  | 'spinbutton'
  | 'status'
  | 'tooltip';
// ARIA 1.2 core role set — the subset Yantra resolves in MVP
```

Cross-references: `LocatorIntent` is the _engine-side_ shape. The wire-protocol form (`LocatorChain` in `packages/protocol`, owned by FEAT-002) is JSON-friendly (no `RegExp` instances — regex is `{ pattern: string, flags: string }`). FEAT-004 owns the JSON ↔ `LocatorIntent` decoder.

#### `LocatorCandidate` — one candidate in a chain

```ts
interface LocatorCandidate {
  readonly intent: LocatorIntent;
  readonly source: 'recorded' | 'authored' | 'reanchored'; // reanchored = Phase 2 only
  readonly notes?: string; // optional human-readable hint from annotate
}
```

#### `LocatorChain` — ordered candidate list, indexed by name in a workflow

```ts
interface LocatorChain {
  readonly name: string; // "Sign in button"
  readonly candidates: readonly LocatorCandidate[]; // ordered: try [0], then [1], …
  readonly strict: boolean; // default true; >1 match throws
}
```

#### `ResolveResult` — success or structured failure

```ts
type ResolveResult =
  | {
      kind: 'success';
      elementHandle: ElementHandle; // puppeteer-core ElementHandle wrapping a CDP objectId
      usedCandidateIndex: number;
      candidatesTried: readonly CandidateAttempt[];
      durationMs: number;
    }
  | {
      kind: 'failure';
      reason: 'not_found' | 'ambiguous' | 'hit_intercepted' | 'not_actionable' | 'frame_detached';
      candidatesTried: readonly CandidateAttempt[];
      lastError?: Error;
      durationMs: number;
    };

interface CandidateAttempt {
  readonly index: number;
  readonly intent: LocatorIntent;
  readonly matchCount: number; // 0, 1, or >1
  readonly outcome: 'matched' | 'no_match' | 'ambiguous' | 'error';
  readonly errorMessage?: string;
  readonly durationMs: number;
}
```

#### `ActionableState` — per-element state used by auto-wait

```ts
interface ActionableState {
  readonly visible: boolean; // bounding rect > 0 AND not display:none/visibility:hidden
  readonly enabled: boolean; // no [disabled] attr, no aria-disabled="true"
  readonly stable: boolean; // bounding rect unchanged for ≥ 100 ms
  readonly receivesEvents: boolean; // elementFromPoint(cx,cy) === el || el.contains(eFP)
  readonly attached: boolean; // still in document
}
```

#### `HitTargetCheckResult` — hit-target interception outcome

```ts
type HitTargetCheckResult =
  | { kind: 'ok'; coordinates: { x: number; y: number } }
  | {
      kind: 'intercepted';
      interceptor: { tagName: string; accessibleName?: string; testid?: string };
      coordinates: { x: number; y: number };
    }
  | { kind: 'outside_viewport'; coordinates: { x: number; y: number } };
```

#### `CandidateRanking` — record-time output (consumed by FEAT-008)

```ts
interface CandidateRanking {
  readonly target: { tagName: string; accessibleName?: string };
  readonly candidates: readonly RankedCandidate[]; // sorted by score descending, capped to topN
}

interface RankedCandidate {
  readonly intent: LocatorIntent;
  readonly score: number; // weight * specificity * stability
  readonly rationale: string; // short string explaining the win, e.g., "data-testid present"
}
```

### Candidate Ranking Weights (record-time emission)

The ranking algorithm in `ranking.ts` produces candidates in this **fixed priority order**, with numeric scores so ties break deterministically. Exact ordering pinned by the plan §7 architecture rules and brainstorm §8.2:

| Rank | Strategy                                                                        | Base weight | When it wins                                        | Notes                                                          |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | `data-testid` (and configurable aliases `data-test-id`, `data-qa`, `data-test`) | **1.00**    | Well-built apps with explicit test hooks            | Highest stability — devs touch testids deliberately            |
| 2    | `role` + accessible name (exact, else regex `/normalize/i`)                     | **0.90**    | Accessible sites; the cross-framework lingua franca | Implicit role (`<button>` → `button`) handled by computed-role |
| 3    | `label-for` / `aria-labelledby` / `aria-label`                                  | **0.75**    | Forms with real `<label for=…>` pairs               | Resolves the labelled element, not the label                   |
| 4    | `placeholder` / `name` attribute                                                | **0.60**    | Unlabeled inputs                                    | Last input-specific fallback                                   |
| 5    | Unique CSS (stable-class heuristic)                                             | **0.45**    | Class names aren't hash-randomized                  | Rejects `/^css-/`, `/^[a-z0-9]{5,}$/`, `/-\d{4,}$/` classes    |
| 6    | Relative anchor (label → next sibling input, heading → following table)         | **0.30**    | Recoverable structural patterns                     | Anchor is itself a `LocatorIntent` — recursive                 |
| 7    | Absolute XPath                                                                  | **0.10**    | Truly last resort                                   | Brittle; emitted because _something_ is better than nothing    |

Specificity multipliers tune within-rank ordering — e.g., a `role+name` candidate with `exact: true` outscores the same role with regex (`× 1.05`); a CSS with two stable classes outscores one with a single class (`× 1.10`). Full multiplier table lives in `ranking.ts` and is property-tested for ordering invariants.

### Repository-Style Interfaces

```ts
interface LocatorResolver {
  /**
   * Resolve a chain against the current page. Walks candidates in order;
   * returns on the first that yields exactly one actionable element (strict mode),
   * or exhausts the chain and returns a structured failure.
   */
  resolve(chain: LocatorChain, options?: ResolveOptions): Promise<ResolveResult>;

  /** Resolve + auto-wait until actionable, returning the success result or throwing one of the typed errors. */
  resolveActionable(chain: LocatorChain, options?: ActionableOptions): Promise<SuccessResult>;
}

interface HitTargetInterceptor {
  /** Verify a synthesized click at (cx, cy) will land on the intended element. */
  check(element: ElementHandle, coords?: { x: number; y: number }): Promise<HitTargetCheckResult>;
}

interface InjectedScriptHost {
  /** Ensures the injected bundle is loaded into the given frame; idempotent. */
  ensureInjected(frameId: string): Promise<void>;

  /** Calls a named export of the injected bundle in the page context. */
  call<T>(frameId: string, fn: keyof InjectedAPI, args: unknown[]): Promise<T>;
}
```

`LocatorResolver` is the **only** locator API the executor (FEAT-005) consumes. `HitTargetInterceptor` is pluggable so integration tests can swap a deterministic stub. `InjectedScriptHost` is the CDP-transport adapter (`Runtime.evaluate` + `Page.createIsolatedWorld` when available).

### Future DB Schema Sketch (Phase 2+ analytics)

When telemetry-to-disk lands (currently `events.jsonl` only), we may want a `locator_resolution_metrics` table for cross-run analysis of locator stability. Not built in MVP; sketched here so the in-memory event shape (TASK-014) is forward-compatible:

```sql
-- Phase 2+ candidate (SQLite, in the per-installation analytics DB)
CREATE TABLE locator_resolution_metrics (
  id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  run_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
  workflow_name   TEXT NOT NULL,
  step_id         TEXT NOT NULL,
  chain_name      TEXT NOT NULL,            -- the named locator, e.g. "Sign in button"
  candidates_tried INTEGER NOT NULL,
  winning_index   INTEGER,                  -- NULL if the chain was exhausted
  outcome         TEXT NOT NULL,            -- 'success' | 'not_found' | 'ambiguous' | 'hit_intercepted' | 'not_actionable'
  duration_ms     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  recorded_at     TEXT NOT NULL             -- ISO-8601
);

CREATE INDEX idx_lrm_workflow_chain ON locator_resolution_metrics (workflow_name, chain_name);
CREATE INDEX idx_lrm_run            ON locator_resolution_metrics (run_id);
```

Use cases (Phase 2+): "which candidates win most for this workflow?" (drives recorder ranking refinement), "is this chain getting flakier over time?" (drift detection), "which sites have the highest fall-through rate past candidate 0?" (DOM-instability indicator).

### Entity Relationships (in-memory)

- `LocatorChain` 1:N `LocatorCandidate` (ordered list)
- `LocatorCandidate` 1:1 `LocatorIntent` (the typed intent)
- `LocatorIntent { kind: "relative" }` recursively contains another `LocatorIntent` (the anchor)
- `ResolveResult.candidatesTried` 1:N `CandidateAttempt` (one per candidate walked)
- A `Workflow` (FEAT-009) owns N named `LocatorChain`s in its `_locators:` block (not modeled here — consumed via FEAT-002 protocol types)

## 3. Files

### Source files (created)

- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/index.ts` — InjectedScript entrypoint. Compiles to the IIFE bundle. Registers `window.__yantra = { resolve, checkState, hitTarget, … }`. **Page context only** — no Node imports.
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/role.ts` — ARIA computed-role + accessible-name algorithm. Ports the relevant parts of Playwright's `roleUtils` (Apache-2.0, attributed). Handles implicit roles (`<button>` → `button`, `<a href>` → `link`, `<input type=text>` → `textbox`).
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/text.ts` — Accessible-name normalization (trim, collapse internal whitespace, optional `toLocaleLowerCase`). Regex matching for `/pattern/flags` intent. Exact vs contains modes.
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/label.ts` — `<label for="x">` + `<input id="x">` pairs; `aria-labelledby` resolution; `aria-label` fallback. Resolves to the _labelled_ element, not the label.
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/testid.ts` — Exact attribute-value match on configurable attribute name list (default `['data-testid', 'data-test-id', 'data-qa', 'data-test']`).
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/css.ts` — Two responsibilities: (a) querying by an arbitrary CSS selector with strict-mode check, (b) the **generator** that walks up the tree producing the shortest selector that uniquely identifies a given element (used at record time by `ranking.ts`).
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/xpath.ts` — Last-resort: query by XPath via `document.evaluate(…)`; generate absolute path via DOM-parent walk.
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/relative.ts` — Resolves `RelativeRelation` against an anchor element. Implements `next-sibling`, `previous-sibling`, `following`, `preceding`, `ancestor`, `descendant`, `labeled-by`.
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/hit-target.ts` — `elementFromPoint(cx, cy)` check; verifies hit lands on the target or a descendant. Returns the intercepting element's tag + accessible name on failure.
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/actionable.ts` — `checkActionableState(el)` returning `ActionableState`. Visibility, enabled, stable (compares bounding rects across a 100ms window), receives-events.
- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/api.ts` — Type declarations of `window.__yantra` namespace (`InjectedAPI`). Shared with Node side via a `.d.ts`-only export path (no runtime import).
- `packages/core/src/locator/resolver.ts` — Node-side `LocatorResolver` implementation. Coordinates `InjectedScriptHost`; serializes `LocatorIntent` to JSON for `Runtime.evaluate`; deserializes `ResolveResult`; emits resolution metrics events.
- `packages/core/src/locator/auto-wait.ts` — `resolveActionable()` polling loop with the Playwright backoff table; integrates with the executor's layer-1 retry budget (passed in via options).
- `packages/core/src/locator/hit-target.ts` — Node-side `HitTargetInterceptor` wrapper around the injected check.
- `packages/core/src/locator/ranking.ts` — Record-time candidate ranking. Pure algorithm callable from inside the InjectedScript (when invoked by the recorder, FEAT-008). Produces `CandidateRanking` sorted by score; cap at `topN` (default 5).
- `packages/core/src/locator/intent-codec.ts` — JSON ↔ `LocatorIntent` codec; converts wire-form regex (`{pattern, flags}`) to/from `RegExp` instances. Single chokepoint so neither side reaches into the other's representation.
- `packages/core/src/locator/errors.ts` — `LocatorNotFoundError`, `LocatorAmbiguousError`, `HitTargetInterceptedError`, `LocatorNotActionableError`, `FrameDetachedError`. All extend `Error` and carry structured `candidatesTried` for the failure report.
- `packages/core/src/locator/build.ts` — esbuild config + invocation script. Builds `injected/index.ts` → `dist/injected.bundle.js` (IIFE format, minified, source-map). Run via `pnpm --filter @yantra/core build:injected`. CI verifies bundle size < 50 KB.
- `packages/core/src/locator/index.ts` — Barrel re-export: `LocatorResolver`, `HitTargetInterceptor`, errors, `LocatorIntent` type. The only file outside `packages/core/src/locator/` should import from is this barrel.

### Test files (created — co-located `*.spec.ts`)

- `packages/core/src/locator/injected/role.spec.ts` — jsdom fixtures: implicit roles, explicit `role` attribute, ARIA computed-role precedence, accessible-name algorithm corner cases.

## 4. Dependencies

### Internal dependencies (must exist before this feature)

- **FEAT-001 (Monorepo Scaffold & CI)** — required for: pnpm workspaces structure, Vitest + `fast-check`, Turborepo build pipeline (the `build:injected` script slots into here), CI matrix (the `@no-llm` test tag must already be respected).
- **FEAT-002 (Yantra Protocol v0)** — required for: the wire-protocol `LocatorChain` Zod schema. This feature's `intent-codec.ts` translates between the protocol's JSON form and the in-memory `LocatorIntent`. If FEAT-002 isn't done, stub the protocol type locally and flag a deviation.
- **FEAT-003 (Chrome Launcher & BrowserProvider)** — required for: a `Page` instance with CDP transport for integration tests. The `InjectedScriptHost` constructor takes a CDP session abstraction owned by FEAT-003. Unit tests use jsdom and don't need FEAT-003.

### External dependencies (new)

- **`esbuild`** (latest stable; LTS-tracked) — bundles the InjectedScript into a single IIFE. `devDependency` of `@yantra/core` only; not a runtime dep.
- **`fast-check`** (latest stable) — already in stack baseline (memory §Testing); used here for ranking-order property tests.

No new heavy runtime dependencies. Specifically **not** adding: `playwright-core` (we intentionally do _not_ depend on Playwright — we port the ideas with attribution), `jsdom` as runtime (only `devDependencies` for unit tests).

### Attribution (license compliance)

The role-resolution algorithm in `role.ts` and the actionable-state checks in `actionable.ts` port specific algorithms from `playwright-core` (Apache-2.0). Attribution headers in each source file cite the upstream files. NOTICE entry added to repo root tracking the port.

### TASK-007: Unique-CSS generator with stable-class heuristic

- [ ] **Implementation**: `packages/core/src/locator/injected/css.ts` — two exports:

  - `generateUniqueCss(el: Element): string | null` — walk up the DOM; at each level prefer (in order): `[id=…]` if stable, `[data-testid=…]` (terminates immediately), `tagname.className1.className2` filtered by stable-class heuristic, `tagname:nth-of-type(n)`. Stop when the accumulated selector is unique in `document`. Returns `null` if no unique selector under depth cap (default 8).

- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc explains the heuristic, lists the regex patterns rejected, documents the depth cap.

### TASK-010: `LocatorResolver.resolve(chain)` Node-side coordinator + chain walk

- [ ] **Implementation**: `packages/core/src/locator/resolver.ts` — class `LocatorResolverImpl implements LocatorResolver`. Constructor takes `InjectedScriptHost` + an event sink (for telemetry, TASK-014). `resolve(chain)` algorithm:
  1. For each candidate in order, encode `intent` to JSON via `intent-codec.ts`.
  2. Call `injectedHost.call(frameId, 'resolveCandidate', [encodedIntent, chain.strict])`. The injected side returns `{ count, objectId? }`.
  3. If `count === 1`: return success with `usedCandidateIndex` and `candidatesTried` so far.
  4. If `count > 1 && chain.strict`: record attempt as `ambiguous`; **do not** continue to next candidate (strict ambiguity is fatal). Return failure.
  5. If `count === 0`: record attempt, try next candidate.
  6. On exhaustion: return `{ kind: "failure", reason: "not_found", candidatesTried, … }`.
  7. Wrap each candidate call with a per-candidate timeout (default 5s) — exceeding it records the attempt as `error` and continues to the next candidate.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `resolver.spec.ts` with a mocked `InjectedScriptHost` — (a) candidate 0 wins → success, `usedCandidateIndex=0`; (b) 0 misses, 1 wins → success, `usedCandidateIndex=1`, both attempts in `candidatesTried`; (c) all miss → `failure.reason="not_found"`; (d) candidate ambiguous in strict mode → `failure.reason="ambiguous"`, walk stops; (e) frame detached mid-walk → `failure.reason="frame_detached"`; (f) per-candidate timeout → attempt recorded as `error`, continues to next.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `resolve` with full algorithm description; `@example` for typical chain walk. Inline comment explaining why ambiguity halts walk (strict mode protects against picking the wrong element silently).
- **Verify**: Six unit-test cases pass with a mocked host.

### TASK-011: Auto-wait — `resolveActionable()` with Playwright backoff

- [ ] **Implementation**: `packages/core/src/locator/auto-wait.ts` — `resolveActionable(chain, options)`:
  1. Determine total deadline from `options.timeoutMs` (default 30000) — this is the **layer-1 locator budget** from the executor (FEAT-005).
  2. Backoff sequence `[0, 20, 50, 100, 100, 500, 500, 500]` then repeating `500`s.
  3. Each tick: call `resolver.resolve(chain)`. On success, call `injected.checkActionableState(objectId)` returning `ActionableState`. If all four state flags are true → return the success result.
  4. On failure with `reason: "ambiguous"` → throw `LocatorAmbiguousError` immediately (non-retriable).
  5. On `not_found` or state-not-ready → continue polling.
  6. Stability check: `checkActionableState` internally compares two bounding-rect snapshots 100 ms apart; if they differ, `stable: false`.
  7. On deadline: throw `LocatorNotActionableError` carrying the last `ActionableState` snapshot for the failure report.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `auto-wait.spec.ts` — using a mock resolver/host that flips state after N ticks: (a) element actionable on first tick → returns immediately; (b) element becomes actionable after 200 ms → returns within 200–300 ms range; (c) element never actionable → throws `LocatorNotActionableError` at the deadline (±50 ms tolerance); (d) ambiguous result short-circuits; (e) `frame_detached` short-circuits with `FrameDetachedError`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc with the four actionable conditions, the backoff sequence, and the deadline semantics. Comment block citing brainstorm §6.3 and the Playwright origin of the backoff table.
- **Verify**: Timing-sensitive tests pass under Vitest's fake-timer mode (`vi.useFakeTimers()`).

### TASK-013: Candidate ranking algorithm (record-time emission)

- [ ] **Implementation**: `packages/core/src/locator/ranking.ts` — `rankCandidates(element: Element, options?: RankingOptions): CandidateRanking`:
  1. Probe the element for each strategy in priority order; for each that yields a viable intent, compute `score = baseWeight * specificityMultiplier * stabilityMultiplier`.
  2. Strategies: testid (each alias attribute), role+name (exact then regex), label-for, placeholder, name-attribute, unique-CSS (only if generator returns non-null), relative-anchor (if a labeled-by or sibling relationship is detectable), absolute-XPath (always available).
  3. Sort descending; cap to `options.topN` (default 5).
  4. **Determinism rule**: ties broken by base weight, then by strategy enum order — never by random / `Math.random()`. Property-test asserts this.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

### Auth

**N/A.** The locator engine is presentation-layer infrastructure; it has no concept of authentication. It runs against whatever DOM the executor has navigated to.

### Error Handling

Every failure mode in this feature has a typed error class — no generic `Error` throws. All errors extend `Error` and carry a structured `candidatesTried: readonly CandidateAttempt[]` field (or equivalent context) so the executor's failure report (FEAT-005, FEAT-010) can render the full attempt history. Errors live in `packages/core/src/locator/errors.ts`:

| Error class                   | Thrown when                                                                              | Carries                                                            |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `LocatorNotFoundError`        | Chain exhausted; every candidate returned 0 matches                                      | `chainName`, `candidatesTried`                                     |
| `LocatorAmbiguousError`       | A candidate returned >1 matches in strict mode                                           | `chainName`, `candidateIndex`, `matchCount`, `candidatesTried`     |
| `HitTargetInterceptedError`   | `elementFromPoint` returned a different element (overlay/modal covers target)            | `chainName`, `interceptor: { tagName, accessibleName? }`, `coords` |
| `LocatorNotActionableError`   | Element resolved but never became visible/stable/enabled/receives-events within deadline | `chainName`, `lastActionableState: ActionableState`, `deadlineMs`  |
| `FrameDetachedError`          | Frame holding the target was detached mid-resolution                                     | `chainName`, `frameId`                                             |
| `LocatorInvalidSelectorError` | CSS/XPath candidate had invalid syntax                                                   | `intent`, `parseError`                                             |

Behavior on errors:

- **Within the resolver itself**: errors are returned as `ResolveResult.failure` from `resolve()`; thrown from `resolveActionable()`.
- **Upstream (executor)**: layer-2 retry (the step-level budget) consumes these errors; on layer-2 exhaustion, the run aborts with a `task_failed` event and a `report.md` (per memory §Error Handling).
- **Bounded re-prompt does NOT apply here** — locator failures aren't agent-validation failures. There is no LLM in this loop in MVP.

### Logging

Per memory §Logging:

- **`debug` level**: every candidate attempted, the resolution duration, the `usedCandidateIndex` on success. Emitted as TaskEvent `locator_resolution` (TASK-014), not as ad-hoc log lines.
- **`warn` level**: when chain falls through past candidate 0 (the recorded primary missed; a fallback won). This is a drift signal worth surfacing.
- **`error` level**: chain exhausted; emitted alongside the `task_failed` event for that step.
- **Pino redactor**: not needed in this feature — locator events carry no values, only structural metadata. The security invariant test (TASK-014 case c) enforces this.

### Security

**InjectedScript runs in the page's JavaScript context — same security boundary as user-authored page scripts.** Two security invariants:

1. **No data exfiltration via the injected layer.** The injected API returns only structural metadata (`count`, `objectId`, `tagName`, `accessibleName`, `usedCandidateIndex`) — **never** raw DOM nodes, `textContent`, `innerHTML`, attribute values (beyond what's needed to identify an intercepting element by tag + accessible name), or form values. CDP `Runtime.evaluate` results are JSON-serialized at the CDP boundary, so accidentally returning a DOM node would surface as a serialization error in CI.
   - **Property test (TASK-014 case c)**: synthesize a `resolve()` call against a page with sensitive form values; assert the event sink's emitted payload, when JSON-stringified, contains none of the sensitive strings.
2. **No `eval` or `Function()` from Node-side input.** The InjectedScript bundle is a pre-compiled IIFE; the Node side calls **named API methods** with JSON-serialized arguments. We do **not** ship arbitrary code strings to `Runtime.evaluate`. The `build.spec.ts` (TASK-001) asserts the bundle contains no dynamic `eval` constructs.

The injected layer **does** see authenticated page content (because it runs _in_ the page). It just doesn't return any of it. The sanitizer (FEAT-006) is a separate layer concerned with LLM-bound payloads; this feature never crosses that boundary.

CDP-pipe transport (owned by FEAT-003) protects against localhost-port attack surface — the locator engine inherits this from its transport dependency.

### Testing

Per memory §Testing — every test in this feature is `@no-llm`. The breakdown:

- **Unit tests (jsdom)** — TASKs 002–009, 013, plus subsets of 010/011/012. Pure-JS algorithms tested against synthetic DOM fixtures.
- **Unit tests (Node, mocked host)** — TASKs 010, 011, 014. The `InjectedScriptHost` is a strategy interface; tests pass a deterministic mock.
- **Property tests (`fast-check`)** — TASK-013 (ranking ordering invariants); TASK-007 (CSS round-trip); TASK-009 (XPath round-trip); intent codec round-trip.
- **Integration tests (real Chrome via FEAT-003)** — `e2e/locator/*.e2e.ts` for timing-sensitive auto-wait + hit-target on a real browser. **Tagged `@requires-chrome`** so they run in the nightly Chrome-pinned matrix, not on every PR. The `@no-llm` tag still applies — these run with `LLM_PROVIDER=none`.

Coverage target: ≥ 90% lines on `resolver.ts`, `auto-wait.ts`, `ranking.ts`, and the injected `role.ts` + `label.ts` (the most likely sources of real-world flake regressions). Glue code (build script, barrel) excluded.
